descriptionChirho: A proper noun identifying both the eighth son of Jacob (by Zilpah, Leah's handmaid) and the Israelite tribe descended from him. Named in Genesis 30:13 with the etiology 'Happy am I!' (be-oshri), connecting the name to the root ashar ('to be happy'). As a tribal name, Asher designates one of the twelve tribes of Israel, with its territory in the northwestern coastal region of Canaan. Appears extensively in tribal lists, census records, territorial allotments, and historical narratives: Genesis 35:26; 46:17; 49:20; Exodus 1:4; Numbers 1:13, 40-41; 2:27; 7:72; 10:26; 13:13; 26:44-47; 34:27; Deuteronomy 27:13; 33:24; Joshua 17:7, 10-11; 19:24, 31, 34; 21:6, 30; Judges 1:31-32; 5:17; 6:35; 7:23; 1 Kings 4:16; 1 Chronicles 2:2; 6:59, 62, 74; 7:30, 40; 12:36; 2 Chronicles 30:11; Ezekiel 48:2-3, 34. Prepositional variants (from Asher, in Asher, to/for Asher) and conjunctive forms are syntactic rather than semantic distinctions, all referring to the same tribal entity or its eponymous ancestor.
